messages:
chen: Quick share — ran a regional sweep for KV cache behavior across us-west / eu-central / apac with three sequence-length mixes (short, mixed, long). H100 vs A100, default LRU, prefetch=16. Putting highlights here, CSVs follow.

maria: awesome — which eviction policy? LRU by default?

chen: yes LRU. prefetch window 16, pager threshold 0.75, spillback enabled, no persistent backing for these runs. runtime fp16.

alex: how's hit rate correlating with p99? got numbers?

chen: short summary:
- short-slen: hitrate 89–92% -> p99 24–28ms (H100 slightly better)
- mixed-slen: hitrate 66–74% -> p99 48–62ms (varies by kernel)
- long-slen: hitrate 31–38% -> p99 140–220ms, lots of paging & DMA stalls

rishi: can you paste the bench command and kernel flags? want to compare CUTLASS vs fused kernels.

chen: sure — command used:
```
bench-run --model redwood/open-7b \
  --backend h100 \
  --kernel fused-attn_v2 \
  --seqlen-mix short,mixed,long \
  --prefetch 16 \
  --evict-policy LRU \
  --out results/us-west_h100.csv
```
Also ran with `--kernel cutlass` and repeated on `--backend a100`.

devon: observed behavior: CUTLASS gave ~15% better throughput when hitrate > 70% (less kernel overhead). fused-attn_v2 wins ~2-3x in low-hit scenarios on H100 because it avoids repeated small kernel launches and reduces paging amplification. A100 favored CUTLASS for fp16 in mixed case.

maria: interesting. any config changes that helped long-slen p99? e.g., bigger prefetch, persistent KV on SSD?

chen: increasing prefetch to 48 improved long-slen p99 by ~20% but increased CPU and memory pressure (more host-side buffering). persistent-KV (local NVMe) lowered p99 by ~30% in long-slen but added cost. Spillback toggles moved the tail — disabling spillback slightly reduced variability but raised average p99 since requests waited for local page loads.

bench-bot: Automated summary:
us-west / H100 / short: throughput 12.5k tok/s, p50 6ms, p95 18ms, p99 27ms, hit 90%
us-west / H100 / mixed: throughput 9.1k tok/s, p99 55ms, hit 70%
us-west / H100 / long: throughput 3.2k tok/s, p99 205ms, hit 34%
(see CSVs attached to job 1725023456)

alex: can we get kernel-level flame traces for the long runs? need to see DMA stall breakdown and where paging is blocking.

chen: uploaded perf traces and flamegraphs -> https://internal/bench/1725023456/traces.zip (contains per-region/hw/kernel breakdown).

rishi: next steps proposal:
- run CLOCK-Pro eviction + hybrid adaptive prefetch (prefetch window tuned by session seqlen histogram) in eu-central on both H100/A100
- add INT8 quantized run for mixed profile (to measure kernel throughput gains vs quality)
- schedule a dedicated-pool canary with spillback disabled to measure tail improvements
I can own CLOCK-Pro + adaptive prefetch prototype.

devon: +1. also add a tiny experiment toggling kernel fuse thresholds (batch size trigger for fused-attn) — that changed behavior in the H100 low-hit tests.

maria: thanks team. I'll assemble a 1-page TL;DR with commands, config, and the bench-bot summary and put it in eng-ml/bench-notes. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: scheduled job bench/cpu-bound/1725023456 -> queued

chen: thanks all — will post CSVs and a short writeup by EOD.
